terrŭlentus , a, um, adj. terra,
I.of or belonging to the earth, earthly (late Lat.): quod terrulentum ac sordidum, etc., Prud. στεφ. 2, 196: “hic (Cain) terrulentis, ille (Abel) vivis fungitur,” i. e. fruits of the earth, id. Hamart. 5 praef. —Adv.: terrŭlentē
in an earthly manner: quaerere rem spiritalem, Prud. στεφ. 10, 378.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
